source: Published name-hash algorithms a Windows program uses to find a function by a 32-bit value instead of by its name. Each entry names the primitive (implemented in maljan.tools.api_hashes), the encoding the name is hashed in, the case it is folded to first, whether its terminating NUL is hashed too, and, for the forms that add a hash of the module's name, how that name is hashed.

algorithms.description: CRC-32 (the zlib/IEEE polynomial, reflected 0xEDB88320) of the ASCII function name
CRC-32 of the lower-cased ASCII function name
CRC-32 of the function name as UTF-16LE
CRC-32 of the lower-cased function name as UTF-16LE
rotate the 32-bit sum right by 13 bits, then add the next byte of the ASCII function name

ror13 of the ASCII function name with its NUL, added to ror13 of the upper-cased UTF-16LE module name with its NUL, the form common position-independent code uses to look a function up in every loaded module at once
djb2 (start at 5381, multiply by 33 and add each byte) of the ASCII function name, 32 bits
djb2 of the lower-cased ASCII function name
Fowler-Noll-Vo, 1a variant, 32-bit (offset basis 0x811C9DC5, prime 0x01000193) of the ASCII function name
Fowler-Noll-Vo, 1a variant, 32-bit, of the lower-cased ASCII function name
